title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Partnership Definition
text:
Partnership Definition

Key terms: Partnership, Profit, Loss, Mutual Agency

A partnership is a business owned by two or more people who agree to share profits and losses. It requires at least two people, an agreement, a business, mutual agency, and sharing of profits and losses.

metadata.subject: Accountancy
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Partnership Definition in Grade 12 Accountancy.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Partnership Deed
text:
Partnership Deed

Key terms: Partnership Deed, Profit-sharing Ratio, Capital Contribution

A partnership deed is a written agreement outlining the terms of a partnership, including profit-sharing ratio, capital contribution, and other rules. It's not required but helps avoid disputes.

metadata.subject: Accountancy
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Partnership Deed in Grade 12 Accountancy.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Partnership Act Provisions
text:
Partnership Act Provisions

Key terms: Indian Partnership Act 1932, Profit Sharing, Interest on Capital

The Indian Partnership Act 1932 provides rules for profit sharing, interest on capital and drawings, and remuneration for partners. If the partnership deed is silent, these provisions apply.

metadata.subject: Accountancy
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Partnership Act Provisions in Grade 12 Accountancy.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Fixed Capital Method
text:
Fixed Capital Method

Key terms: Fixed Capital Method, Capital Account, Current Account

In the fixed capital method, partners' capital remains constant unless changed. Profit, loss, and other adjustments are recorded in a separate current account.

metadata.subject: Accountancy
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Fixed Capital Method in Grade 12 Accountancy.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Fluctuating Capital Method
text:
Fluctuating Capital Method

Key terms: Fluctuating Capital Method, Capital Account, Adjustments

In the fluctuating capital method, all adjustments are recorded directly in the partners' capital accounts, causing the balance to fluctuate.

metadata.subject: Accountancy
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Fluctuating Capital Method in Grade 12 Accountancy.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Fluctuating Capital Method
text:
Fluctuating Capital Method

Key terms: capital account, drawings, interest on capital

A method of accounting for partners' capital where the capital account balance fluctuates from year to year, reflecting changes in the partners' investments and withdrawals.

metadata.subject: Accountancy
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Fluctuating Capital Method in Grade 12 Accountancy.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Profit and Loss Appropriation Account
text:
Profit and Loss Appropriation Account

Key terms: net profit, interest on capital, share of profit

An account that shows how the profits or losses of a partnership are distributed among the partners after making necessary adjustments such as interest on capital, salary, and commission.

metadata.subject: Accountancy
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Profit and Loss Appropriation Account in Grade 12 Accountancy.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Partner's Capital Account
text:
Partner's Capital Account

Key terms: capital, drawings, interest on capital, share of profit

An account that records the initial investment, additional capital, drawings, interest on capital, and the partner's share of profit or loss for a partner in a partnership firm.

metadata.subject: Accountancy
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to remember concepts related to Partner's Capital Account in Grade 12 Accountancy.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Partner's Current Account
text:
Partner's Current Account

Key terms: drawings, interest on drawings, salary, commission, share of profit

An account that records the partner's drawings, interest on drawings, salary, commission, and the partner's share of profit or loss for a partner in a partnership firm.

metadata.subject: Accountancy
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to remember concepts related to Partner's Current Account in Grade 12 Accountancy.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Distribution of Profit among Partners
text:
Distribution of Profit among Partners

Key terms: profit sharing ratio, net profit, share of profit

The process of dividing the profits or losses of a partnership firm among the partners in their agreed ratio or equally if no ratio is specified.

metadata.subject: Accountancy
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Distribution of Profit among Partners in Grade 12 Accountancy.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Interest on Capital
text:
Interest on Capital

Key terms: capital, interest rate, capital account

The amount of money earned by a partner for using their capital in the partnership business, calculated as a percentage of the capital invested.

metadata.subject: Accountancy
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Interest on Capital in Grade 12 Accountancy.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Interest on Drawings
text:
Interest on Drawings

Key terms: drawings, interest rate, partner's current account

The amount of money charged to a partner for withdrawing money from the partnership business, calculated as a percentage of the drawings.

metadata.subject: Accountancy
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Interest on Drawings in Grade 12 Accountancy.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Salary to Partner
text:
Salary to Partner

Key terms: partner, salary, partner's current account

The amount of money paid to a partner for the services they provide to the partnership business, recorded as an expense in the partner's current account.

metadata.subject: Accountancy
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Salary to Partner in Grade 12 Accountancy.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Interest on Capital Calculation
text:
Interest on Capital Calculation

Key terms: capital, interest, addition, withdrawal

Interest on capital is calculated based on the average capital invested by partners during a financial year. It's calculated at the agreed rate and time period, considering any additions or withdrawals of capital.

metadata.subject: Accountancy
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Interest on Capital Calculation in Grade 12 Accountancy.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Interest on Drawings
text:
Interest on Drawings

Key terms: drawings, interest, time period, agreed rate

Interest on drawings is charged to partners who withdraw money from the firm for personal use. It's calculated based on the amount withdrawn and the time period it was outstanding, at an agreed rate.

metadata.subject: Accountancy
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Interest on Drawings in Grade 12 Accountancy.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Profit Sharing without Interest on Capital
text:
Profit Sharing without Interest on Capital

Key terms: profit, sharing, agreement, capital

In the absence of an agreement, profits are shared among partners based on their profit-sharing ratio, and no interest on capital is paid.

metadata.subject: Accountancy
metadata.topic: Profit Sharing without Interest on Capital
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Profit Sharing without Interest on Capital in Grade 12 Accountancy.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Profit Sharing with Interest on Capital
text:
Profit Sharing with Interest on Capital

Key terms: profit, sharing, agreement, capital, interest

When there's an agreement to pay interest on capital, profits are shared among partners after deducting the agreed interest on capital.

metadata.subject: Accountancy
metadata.topic: Profit Sharing with Interest on Capital
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Profit Sharing with Interest on Capital in Grade 12 Accountancy.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Interest on Capital when Profit is Less
text:
Interest on Capital when Profit is Less

Key terms: interest, capital, profit, distribution

If the profit earned is less than the amount of interest on capital due, the interest paid is restricted to the amount of profit. Profit is then effectively distributed based on the ratio of interest on capital.

metadata.subject: Accountancy
metadata.topic: Interest on Capital when Profit is Less
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to analyze concepts related to Interest on Capital when Profit is Less in Grade 12 Accountancy.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Interest on Drawings Calculation (Fixed Monthly Withdrawals)
text:
Interest on Drawings Calculation (Fixed Monthly Withdrawals)

Key terms: drawings, interest, average period, withdrawal

Interest on drawings is calculated based on the average period for which the amount was withdrawn, considering whether it was withdrawn at the beginning, middle, or end of the month.

metadata.subject: Accountancy
metadata.topic: Interest on Drawings Calculation (Fixed Monthly Withdrawals)
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Interest on Drawings Calculation (Fixed Monthly Withdrawals) in Grade 12 Accountancy.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Interest on Drawings Calculation (Quarterly Withdrawals)
text:
Interest on Drawings Calculation (Quarterly Withdrawals)

Key terms: drawings, interest, total amount, time period

Interest on drawings is calculated based on the total amount withdrawn during the year and the time period it was outstanding, considering whether it was withdrawn at the beginning or end of each quarter.

metadata.subject: Accountancy
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Interest on Drawings Calculation (Quarterly Withdrawals) in Grade 12 Accountancy.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Interest on Partner's Capital
text:
Interest on Partner's Capital

Key terms: capital, interest, profit-sharing ratio

Interest is calculated on each partner's capital at a specified rate. It is distributed among partners in their profit-sharing ratio.

metadata.subject: Accountancy
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Interest on Partner's Capital in Grade 12 Accountancy.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Interest on Drawings
text:
Interest on Drawings

Key terms: drawings, product method, average period method

Interest on drawings is calculated on the amount withdrawn by a partner for personal use, for the period it was withdrawn. It is calculated using the product method or average period method.

metadata.subject: Accountancy
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Interest on Drawings in Grade 12 Accountancy.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Guarantee of Profit to a Partner
text:
Guarantee of Profit to a Partner

Key terms: guarantee, deficiency, profit-sharing ratio

Sometimes, a partner is guaranteed a minimum profit share. Any deficiency is borne by the guaranteeing partners in their profit-sharing ratio.

metadata.subject: Accountancy
metadata.topic: Guarantee of Profit to a Partner
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to analyze concepts related to Guarantee of Profit to a Partner in Grade 12 Accountancy.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Profit Distribution in Partnership
text:
Profit Distribution in Partnership

Key terms: Profit Sharing Ratio, Guaranteed Profit, Deficiency

In a partnership, profits are distributed among partners based on their agreed ratio. This ratio can be changed, and any deficiency in profit can be shared by guaranteeing partners.

metadata.subject: Accountancy
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Profit Distribution in Partnership in Grade 12 Accountancy.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Interest on Capital and Drawings
text:
Interest on Capital and Drawings

Key terms: Interest on Capital, Interest on Drawings, Average Capital, Average Drawings

Partners may be entitled to interest on their capital and charged interest on their drawings. These amounts are calculated based on the average capital and drawings for the period.

metadata.subject: Accountancy
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Interest on Capital and Drawings in Grade 12 Accountancy.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Past Adjustments in Partnership
text:
Past Adjustments in Partnership

Key terms: Profit and Loss Adjustment Account, Past Adjustments, Capital Accounts

Errors or omissions in recording transactions can be corrected through 'Profit and Loss Adjustment Account' or directly in partners' capital accounts.

metadata.subject: Accountancy
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Past Adjustments in Partnership in Grade 12 Accountancy.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Admission of a New Partner
text:
Admission of a New Partner

Key terms: New Partner, Guaranteed Amount, Deficiency

A new partner can be admitted with a guaranteed amount, and the liability for any deficiency is borne by the existing partners in their profit sharing ratio.

metadata.subject: Accountancy
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Admission of a New Partner in Grade 12 Accountancy.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Capital Accounts in Partnership
text:
Capital Accounts in Partnership

Key terms: Capital Accounts, Fixed Capital Method, Fluctuating Capital Method

Capital accounts record partners' investments, drawings, and their share of profits or losses. They can be maintained using fixed or fluctuating capital methods.

metadata.subject: Accountancy
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to remember concepts related to Capital Accounts in Partnership in Grade 12 Accountancy.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Interest on Partner's Loan
text:
Interest on Partner's Loan

Key terms: Partner's Loan, Interest on Loan, Partnership Deed

If a partner lends money to the firm, they are entitled to interest on that loan, usually at a rate specified in the partnership deed or by law.

metadata.subject: Accountancy
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Interest on Partner's Loan in Grade 12 Accountancy.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Salary or Commission to Partners
text:
Salary or Commission to Partners

Key terms: Salary, Commission, Partnership Deed

Partners may be entitled to a salary or commission for their services to the firm, which is usually specified in the partnership deed.

metadata.subject: Accountancy
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Salary or Commission to Partners in Grade 12 Accountancy.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Profit Sharing in Partnership
text:
Profit Sharing in Partnership

Key terms: Profit, Partnership, Profit Sharing Ratio

In a partnership, profits are shared among partners based on their agreed ratio, which can be equal or in proportion to their capital contributions.

metadata.subject: Accountancy
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Profit Sharing in Partnership in Grade 12 Accountancy.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Interest on Capital in Partnership
text:
Interest on Capital in Partnership

Key terms: Interest, Capital, Partnership Agreement

Partners are entitled to receive interest on their capital contributions, usually at a predetermined rate, as per the partnership agreement.

metadata.subject: Accountancy
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Interest on Capital in Partnership in Grade 12 Accountancy.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Salary to Partners in Partnership
text:
Salary to Partners in Partnership

Key terms: Salary, Partners, Partnership Deed

Partners may receive a salary for managing the business, as agreed in the partnership deed, which is then deducted from the profits.

metadata.subject: Accountancy
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Salary to Partners in Partnership in Grade 12 Accountancy.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Interest on Drawings in Partnership
text:
Interest on Drawings in Partnership

Key terms: Interest, Drawings, Partnership Agreement

Interest is charged on partners' drawings (withdrawals) from the firm, usually at a rate specified in the partnership agreement.

metadata.subject: Accountancy
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Interest on Drawings in Partnership in Grade 12 Accountancy.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Minimum Profit Guarantee to Partners
text:
Minimum Profit Guarantee to Partners

Key terms: Minimum Profit, Guarantee, Partners

Some partners may be guaranteed a minimum share of the profits, even if the total profits are less than the guaranteed amount.

metadata.subject: Accountancy
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Minimum Profit Guarantee to Partners in Grade 12 Accountancy.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Adjusting Capital Contributions in Partnership
text:
Adjusting Capital Contributions in Partnership

Key terms: Capital Contributions, Adjustment, Average Capital

Partners may adjust their capital contributions during the year, and interest on capital is calculated based on the average capital contribution.

metadata.subject: Accountancy
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Adjusting Capital Contributions in Partnership in Grade 12 Accountancy.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Omitted Interest on Capital in Partnership
text:
Omitted Interest on Capital in Partnership

Key terms: Omitted Interest, Capital, Interest Rate

If interest on capital is omitted in the accounts, it can be calculated based on the capital balances and the applicable interest rate.

metadata.subject: Accountancy
metadata.topic: Omitted Interest on Capital in Partnership
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Omitted Interest on Capital in Partnership in Grade 12 Accountancy.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Interest on Drawings Based on Withdrawal Timing
text:
Interest on Drawings Based on Withdrawal Timing

Key terms: Interest, Drawings, Withdrawal Timing

The timing of partners' drawings (withdrawals) affects the calculation of interest on drawings, as it determines the number of months the amount was withdrawn.

metadata.subject: Accountancy
metadata.topic: Interest on Drawings Based on Withdrawal Timing
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to analyze concepts related to Interest on Drawings Based on Withdrawal Timing in Grade 12 Accountancy.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Interest on Capital Calculation
text:
Interest on Capital Calculation

Key terms: capital account, interest on capital, profit distribution

Interest on capital is calculated based on the balance in the capital account at the end of the year. It is usually calculated at a pre-agreed rate and is added to the profit before distribution among partners.

metadata.subject: Accountancy
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Interest on Capital Calculation in Grade 12 Accountancy.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Profit Sharing Ratio
text:
Profit Sharing Ratio

Key terms: profit sharing ratio, profit distribution, capital contribution

Profit sharing ratio is the ratio in which profits and losses are distributed among partners. It can be based on capital contribution, time spent, or other agreed terms.

metadata.subject: Accountancy
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Profit Sharing Ratio in Grade 12 Accountancy.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Guaranteed Minimum Profit
text:
Guaranteed Minimum Profit

Key terms: guaranteed minimum profit, deficiency, profit distribution

Some partners may have a guaranteed minimum profit, which means they are assured of a certain amount of profit, regardless of the actual profit earned. Any deficiency is borne by the other partners.

metadata.subject: Accountancy
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Guaranteed Minimum Profit in Grade 12 Accountancy.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Interest on Drawings
text:
Interest on Drawings

Key terms: drawings, interest on drawings, profit distribution

Interest on drawings is calculated on the amount of drawings taken by a partner during the year. It is usually calculated at a pre-agreed rate and is deducted from the partner's share of profit.

metadata.subject: Accountancy
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Interest on Drawings in Grade 12 Accountancy.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Profit and Loss Appropriation Account
text:
Profit and Loss Appropriation Account

Key terms: profit and loss appropriation account, net profit, profit distribution

A profit and loss appropriation account is a statement that shows how the net profit or loss of a partnership firm is divided among the partners. It includes adjustments for interest on capital, interest on drawings, and other relevant items.

metadata.subject: Accountancy
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Profit and Loss Appropriation Account in Grade 12 Accountancy.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Adjustment Entries
text:
Adjustment Entries

Key terms: adjustment entries, errors, omissions, financial statements

Adjustment entries are made to correct errors or omissions in the accounts. They ensure that the financial statements accurately reflect the financial position of the firm.

metadata.subject: Accountancy
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Adjustment Entries in Grade 12 Accountancy.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Change in Profit Sharing Ratio
text:
Change in Profit Sharing Ratio

Key terms: change in profit sharing ratio, capital contribution, profit distribution

The profit sharing ratio can change over time due to changes in capital contribution, time spent, or other agreed terms. Any change in the ratio should be reflected in the distribution of profits.

metadata.subject: Accountancy
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Change in Profit Sharing Ratio in Grade 12 Accountancy.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Average Interest on Drawings
text:
Average Interest on Drawings

Key terms: average interest on drawings, drawings, interest calculation

When the exact period of drawings is not known, interest on drawings is calculated on an average basis. This is done by assuming that the drawings were taken for the entire year.

metadata.subject: Accountancy
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Average Interest on Drawings in Grade 12 Accountancy.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Reconstitution of a Partnership Firm
text:
Reconstitution of a Partnership Firm

Key terms: partnership agreement, reconstitution, new partner, profit sharing ratio

End of existing partnership agreement, new agreement with changed relationship among members. Can happen due to admission of new partner, change in profit sharing ratio, retirement or death of a partner.

metadata.subject: Accountancy
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to remember concepts related to Reconstitution of a Partnership Firm in Grade 12 Accountancy.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Admission of a New Partner
text:
Admission of a New Partner

Key terms: new partner, capital, goodwill, profit sharing ratio

New partner brings capital and/or managerial help, acquires share in assets and profits, requires premium or goodwill for super profits.

metadata.subject: Accountancy
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Admission of a New Partner in Grade 12 Accountancy.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | New Profit Sharing Ratio
text:
New Profit Sharing Ratio

Key terms: new partner, profit sharing ratio, old partners

Changes when a new partner is admitted, depends on how new partner acquires share from old partners.

metadata.subject: Accountancy
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to New Profit Sharing Ratio in Grade 12 Accountancy.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Sacrificing Ratio
text:
Sacrificing Ratio

Key terms: old partners, sacrificing ratio, incoming partner

Ratio in which old partners agree to sacrifice their share of profit in favor of the incoming partner.

metadata.subject: Accountancy
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Sacrificing Ratio in Grade 12 Accountancy.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Goodwill
text:
Goodwill

Key terms: goodwill, reputation, super profits

Value of a firm's reputation and business connections, exists only when the firm earns super profits.

metadata.subject: Accountancy
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Goodwill in Grade 12 Accountancy.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Factors Affecting Goodwill
text:
Factors Affecting Goodwill

Key terms: goodwill, factors, value

Nature of business, location, efficiency of management, market conditions, and legal rights affect the value of goodwill.

metadata.subject: Accountancy
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to analyze concepts related to Factors Affecting Goodwill in Grade 12 Accountancy.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Methods of Valuation of Goodwill
text:
Methods of Valuation of Goodwill

Key terms: goodwill, valuation, capitalization, turnover

Capitalization of super profits, multiple of turnover, or comparison with similar businesses can be used to value goodwill.

metadata.subject: Accountancy
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to evaluate concepts related to Methods of Valuation of Goodwill in Grade 12 Accountancy.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Treatment of Goodwill on Admission of a New Partner
text:
Treatment of Goodwill on Admission of a New Partner

Key terms: goodwill, admission, new partner, premium

Goodwill is treated as an asset, shared by existing partners in sacrificing ratio, new partner pays premium for goodwill.

metadata.subject: Accountancy
metadata.topic: Treatment of Goodwill on Admission of a New Partner
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to create concepts related to Treatment of Goodwill on Admission of a New Partner in Grade 12 Accountancy.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Factors Affecting Goodwill Value
text:
Factors Affecting Goodwill Value

Key terms: Nature of business, Location, Efficiency of management, Market situation, Special advantages

Goodwill value is influenced by the nature of business, location, management efficiency, market situation, and special advantages.

metadata.subject: Accountancy
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to remember concepts related to Factors Affecting Goodwill Value in Grade 12 Accountancy.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Need for Valuation of Goodwill
text:
Need for Valuation of Goodwill

Key terms: Sale of business, Change in profit-sharing ratio, Admission of new partner, Retirement or death of a partner, Dissolution of the firm

Goodwill valuation is necessary at the time of sale of a business or changes in partnership, such as change in profit-sharing ratio, admission of new partner, retirement or death of a partner, or dissolution of the firm.

metadata.subject: Accountancy
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Need for Valuation of Goodwill in Grade 12 Accountancy.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Methods of Valuation of Goodwill
text:
Methods of Valuation of Goodwill

Key terms: Average profits method, Super profits method, Capitalisation method

Goodwill can be valued using various methods, such as average profits method, super profits method, and capitalisation method.

metadata.subject: Accountancy
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Methods of Valuation of Goodwill in Grade 12 Accountancy.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Average Profits Method
text:
Average Profits Method

Key terms: Years' purchase, Average profits

In this method, goodwill is valued at an agreed number of 'years' purchase of the average profits of the past few years.

metadata.subject: Accountancy
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Average Profits Method in Grade 12 Accountancy.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Super Profits Method
text:
Super Profits Method

Key terms: Super profits, Normal profits, Years' purchase

This method values goodwill based on the excess profits (super profits) over the normal profits, multiplied by a certain number of years' purchase.

metadata.subject: Accountancy
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Super Profits Method in Grade 12 Accountancy.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Capitalisation Method
text:
Capitalisation Method

Key terms: Capitalisation, Average profits, Super profits, Normal rate of return

Goodwill can be calculated by capitalising the average profits or super profits, based on the normal rate of return.

metadata.subject: Accountancy
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Capitalisation Method in Grade 12 Accountancy.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Treatment of Goodwill
text:
Treatment of Goodwill

Key terms: Premium for goodwill, Ratio of sacrifice

The incoming partner pays a premium for goodwill to the existing partners, which is shared based on their ratio of sacrifice.

metadata.subject: Accountancy
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to evaluate concepts related to Treatment of Goodwill in Grade 12 Accountancy.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Admission of a Partner with Goodwill
text:
Admission of a Partner with Goodwill

Key terms: goodwill, premium for goodwill, sacrificing ratio

When a new partner joins, they may bring goodwill (premium) to compensate existing partners for loss of super profits. This goodwill is shared among existing partners in their profit-sharing ratio.

metadata.subject: Accountancy
metadata.topic: Admission of a Partner with Goodwill
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Admission of a Partner with Goodwill in Grade 12 Accountancy.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Journal Entries for Goodwill
text:
Journal Entries for Goodwill

Key terms: journal entries, capital account, sacrificing ratio

Journal entries are passed to record the admission of a new partner bringing goodwill. The goodwill is first credited to the new partner's capital account, then transferred to the existing partners' capital accounts in their sacrificing ratio.

metadata.subject: Accountancy
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Journal Entries for Goodwill in Grade 12 Accountancy.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Withdrawal of Goodwill
text:
Withdrawal of Goodwill

Key terms: withdrawal, capital account, bank account

Existing partners can withdraw their share of goodwill, either fully or partially. Journal entries are passed to record this withdrawal, debiting the existing partners' capital accounts and crediting the bank account.

metadata.subject: Accountancy
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Withdrawal of Goodwill in Grade 12 Accountancy.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Goodwill Already in Books
text:
Goodwill Already in Books

Key terms: existing goodwill, write-off, old profit-sharing ratio

If goodwill already exists in the books, it is written off at the time of a new partner's admission. The new partner brings in their share of goodwill, and the existing goodwill is shared among the existing partners in their old profit-sharing ratio.

metadata.subject: Accountancy
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to analyze concepts related to Goodwill Already in Books in Grade 12 Accountancy.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | New Partner Doesn't Bring Goodwill
text:
New Partner Doesn't Bring Goodwill

Key terms: new partner's current account, sacrificing ratio, write-off

If a new partner doesn't bring goodwill, the goodwill is debited to their current account and credited to the existing partners' capital accounts in their sacrificing ratio. If goodwill already exists in the books, it is written off first.

metadata.subject: Accountancy
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to New Partner Doesn't Bring Goodwill in Grade 12 Accountancy.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Accounting Standard 26: Intangible Assets
text:
Accounting Standard 26: Intangible Assets

Key terms: intangible assets, AS 26, purchased goodwill, self-generated goodwill

AS 26 defines intangible assets and provides guidelines for their recognition, measurement, and disclosure. Purchased goodwill can be an intangible asset, while self-generated goodwill is not recognized as an asset.

metadata.subject: Accountancy
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Accounting Standard 26: Intangible Assets in Grade 12 Accountancy.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Admission of New Partner
text:
Admission of New Partner

Key terms: goodwill, capital account, reconstituted

When a new partner joins, the old firm continues, and the old partnership is reconstituted. The new partner's capital and share of goodwill are recorded, and the old partners' capital accounts are credited with their share of goodwill.

metadata.subject: Accountancy
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Admission of New Partner in Grade 12 Accountancy.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Transfer of General Reserve
text:
Transfer of General Reserve

Key terms: general reserve, capital account, profit-sharing ratio

At the time of a new partner's admission, the general reserve appearing in the old balance sheet is transferred to the old partners' capital accounts in their old profit-sharing ratio.

metadata.subject: Accountancy
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Transfer of General Reserve in Grade 12 Accountancy.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Revaluation of Assets and Liabilities
text:
Revaluation of Assets and Liabilities

Key terms: revaluation, assets, liabilities, capital account, profit-sharing ratio

Admission of a Partner

metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Admission of a Partner in Grade 12 Accountancy.

Revaluation of Assets

Adjustment of Partners' Capitals

metadata.subject: Accountancy

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Treatment of Goodwill on Admission
text:
Treatment of Goodwill on Admission

metadata.subject: Accountancy
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to evaluate concepts related to Treatment of Goodwill on Admission in Grade 12 Accountancy.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Provision for Doubtful Debts
text:
Provision for Doubtful Debts

A provision for doubtful debts is created based on a percentage of debtors, and is recorded in the profit and loss account.

metadata.subject: Accountancy
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Provision for Doubtful Debts in Grade 12 Accountancy.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Adjustment for Appreciation/Depreciation
text:
Adjustment for Appreciation/Depreciation

Assets and liabilities are adjusted for appreciation or depreciation, and the difference is recorded in a revaluation account.

Opening Balance Sheet

Adjusting Partners' Capital Accounts for Revaluation

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Admitting a New Partner with a Profit Share
text:
Admitting a New Partner with a Profit Share

Recording Revaluation of Assets

metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Recording Revaluation of Assets in Grade 12 Accountancy.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Calculating Goodwill on Admission of a New Partner
text:
Calculating Goodwill on Admission of a New Partner

text:

metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Gaining Ratio in Grade 12 Accountancy.

metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Treatment of Goodwill in Grade 12 Accountancy.

text:
Revaluation of Assets and Liabilities

Adjusting the value of assets and liabilities at the time of retirement/death, and allocating the gain/loss to the partners' capital accounts based on their new profit sharing ratio.

Adjustment of Accumulated Profits/Losses

metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Adjustment of Accumulated Profits/Losses in Grade 12 Accountancy.

metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to create concepts related to Settlement of Amounts Due in Grade 12 Accountancy.

Modes of Dissolution of Partnership

Key terms: change in profit ratio, admission of new partner, retirement/death of partner, insolvency, completion of venture, expiry of partnership period

Partnership can be dissolved by change in profit-sharing ratio, admission of new partner, retirement or death of a partner, insolvency, completion of venture, or expiry of partnership period.

metadata.subject: Accountancy
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Modes of Dissolution of Partnership in Grade 12 Accountancy.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Dissolution of Firm
text:
Dissolution of Firm

Key terms: dissolution by agreement, compulsory dissolution, contingencies

Firm can be dissolved by agreement, court order, insolvency, illegality, or happening of certain contingencies.

metadata.subject: Accountancy
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Dissolution of Firm in Grade 12 Accountancy.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Settlement of Accounts on Dissolution
text:
Settlement of Accounts on Dissolution

Key terms: settlement of accounts, payment of debts, partner's loans, capital distribution

On dissolution, firm's assets are used to pay debts, partner's loans, capital, and then distributed among partners. Private debts and firm's debts are settled in a specific order.

metadata.subject: Accountancy
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Settlement of Accounts on Dissolution in Grade 12 Accountancy.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Realisation Account
text:
Realisation Account

Key terms: realisation account, sale of assets, payment of liabilities, realisation expenses

Realisation account is prepared to record the sale of assets, payment of liabilities, and realisation expenses. The balance is transferred to partners' capital accounts.

metadata.subject: Accountancy
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to create concepts related to Realisation Account in Grade 12 Accountancy.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Transfer of Assets to Realisation Account
text:
Transfer of Assets to Realisation Account

Key terms: Realisation Account, book values, sundry debtors, provision for doubtful debts

All assets (except cash, bank, and fictitious assets) are transferred to the debit side of the Realisation Account at their book values. Sundry debtors are transferred at gross value, and provision for doubtful debts is transferred to the credit side of the Realisation Account.

metadata.subject: Accountancy
metadata.topic: Transfer of Assets to Realisation Account
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Transfer of Assets to Realisation Account in Grade 12 Accountancy.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Transfer of Liabilities to Realisation Account
text:
Transfer of Liabilities to Realisation Account

Key terms: Realisation Account, external liabilities, provisions

All external liability accounts, including provisions, are closed by transferring them to the credit side of the Realisation Account.

metadata.subject: Accountancy
metadata.topic: Transfer of Liabilities to Realisation Account
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Transfer of Liabilities to Realisation Account in Grade 12 Accountancy.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Transfer of Profit/Loss on Realisation
text:
Transfer of Profit/Loss on Realisation

Key terms: profit on realisation, loss on realisation, profit-sharing ratio, equal ratio

In case of profit on realisation, the profit is transferred to the partners' capital accounts in their profit-sharing ratio. In case of loss on realisation, the loss is transferred to the partners' capital accounts in equal ratio.

metadata.subject: Accountancy
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Transfer of Profit/Loss on Realisation in Grade 12 Accountancy.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Partner's Liability for Dissolution Expenses
text:
Partner's Liability for Dissolution Expenses

Key terms: dissolution expenses, partner's capital account

If a partner agrees to bear the dissolution expenses, the amount paid by the firm is debited to the partner's capital account. If the partner pays the expenses themselves, no entry is required.

metadata.subject: Accountancy
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Partner's Liability for Dissolution Expenses in Grade 12 Accountancy.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Remuneration for Dissolution Work
text:
Remuneration for Dissolution Work

Key terms: remuneration, partner's capital account

Remuneration given to a partner for looking after the dissolution work is credited to the partner's capital account.

metadata.subject: Accountancy
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Remuneration for Dissolution Work in Grade 12 Accountancy.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Transfer of Unrecorded Assets/Liabilities
text:
Transfer of Unrecorded Assets/Liabilities

Key terms: Realisation Account, Bank Account, unrecorded assets, unrecorded liabilities

Any unrecorded assets are transferred to the Realisation Account, and any unrecorded liabilities are transferred to the Bank Account.

metadata.subject: Accountancy
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Transfer of Unrecorded Assets/Liabilities in Grade 12 Accountancy.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Payment of Loans Due to Partners
text:
Payment of Loans Due to Partners

Key terms: partner's loan account, bank account

Loans due to partners are paid by debiting the partner's loan account and crediting the bank account.

metadata.subject: Accountancy
metadata.topic: Payment of Loans Due to Partners
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Payment of Loans Due to Partners in Grade 12 Accountancy.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Settlement of Partners' Accounts
text:
Settlement of Partners' Accounts

Key terms: partner's capital account, bank account

If a partner's capital account shows a debit balance, the firm brings in the necessary cash, and the entry is made by debiting the bank account and crediting the partner's capital account. If the partner's capital account shows a credit balance, the balance is paid to the partner, and the entry is made by debiting the partner's capital account and crediting the bank account.

metadata.subject: Accountancy
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Settlement of Partners' Accounts in Grade 12 Accountancy.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Asset Realisation in Dissolution
text:
Asset Realisation in Dissolution

Key terms: Realisation Account, Profit on Realisation, Loss on Realisation

When a partnership firm dissolves, assets are sold and their values are recorded in the Realisation Account. The difference between the sale proceeds and the book value is the profit or loss on realisation.

metadata.subject: Accountancy
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Asset Realisation in Dissolution in Grade 12 Accountancy.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Liability Settlement in Dissolution
text:
Liability Settlement in Dissolution

Key terms: Creditors, Discount on Settlement, Realisation Account

In dissolution, liabilities are settled by paying off creditors. The amount paid is recorded in the Realisation Account, and any discount received is also recorded as a gain.

metadata.subject: Accountancy
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Liability Settlement in Dissolution in Grade 12 Accountancy.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Partner's Capital Account Settlement
text:
Partner's Capital Account Settlement

Key terms: Partner's Capital Account, Partner's Loan Account, Profit/Loss Transfer

Upon dissolution, partners' capital accounts are settled by transferring the balance to the partners' loan or capital accounts, as applicable. Any profit or loss is also transferred to these accounts.

metadata.subject: Accountancy
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Partner's Capital Account Settlement in Grade 12 Accountancy.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Bank Account in Dissolution
text:
Bank Account in Dissolution

Key terms: Bank Account, Cash Receipts, Cash Payments

The Bank Account is used to record the receipts and payments made during the dissolution process. It helps in tracking the cash inflows and outflows.

metadata.subject: Accountancy
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Bank Account in Dissolution in Grade 12 Accountancy.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Realisation Expenses
text:
Realisation Expenses

Key terms: Realisation Expenses, Realisation Account, Costs Incurred

Realisation expenses are the costs incurred during the dissolution process, such as legal fees, auctioneer's commission, or advertisement expenses. These are recorded in the Realisation Account.

metadata.subject: Accountancy
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Realisation Expenses in Grade 12 Accountancy.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Unexpired Insurance in Dissolution
text:
Unexpired Insurance in Dissolution

Key terms: Unexpired Insurance, Net Recoverable Amount, Realisation Account

If a partnership firm has unexpired insurance, the net recoverable amount is calculated and recorded in the Realisation Account. The premium already paid is treated as an asset.

metadata.subject: Accountancy
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Unexpired Insurance in Dissolution in Grade 12 Accountancy.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Provision for Doubtful Debts in Dissolution
text:
Provision for Doubtful Debts in Dissolution

Key terms: Provision for Doubtful Debts, Realisation Account, Gain on Recovery

When a partnership firm dissolves, any provision for doubtful debts is transferred to the Realisation Account. If the amount recovered is more than the provision, the excess is recorded as a gain.

metadata.subject: Accountancy
metadata.topic: Provision for Doubtful Debts in Dissolution
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Provision for Doubtful Debts in Dissolution in Grade 12 Accountancy.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Partner's Loan in Dissolution
text:
Partner's Loan in Dissolution

Key terms: Partner's Loan, Realisation Account, Partner's Capital Account

In dissolution, partner's loans are either paid off or transferred to the partner's capital account. If the loan is paid off, the amount is recorded in the Realisation Account. If it's transferred, the balance is transferred to the partner's capital account.

metadata.subject: Accountancy
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Partner's Loan in Dissolution in Grade 12 Accountancy.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Dissolution of Partnership Firm
text:
Dissolution of Partnership Firm

The process of ending a partnership business, settling all accounts, and distributing assets and liabilities among partners.

metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Dissolution of Partnership Firm in Grade 12 Accountancy.

Realisation Account

An account used to record the transactions related to the sale and realisation of assets and settlement of liabilities during the dissolution of a partnership firm.

metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to apply concepts related to Realisation Account in Grade 12 Accountancy.

Order of Settlement of Accounts

The sequence in which accounts are settled during the dissolution of a partnership firm: creditors, partners' loans, partners' capital, and profit/loss.

text:
Realisation Expenses

Costs incurred during the dissolution of a partnership firm, such as legal fees, auctioneer's commission, and other expenses related to the realisation of assets and settlement of liabilities.

metadata.subject: Accountancy
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to remember concepts related to Realisation Expenses in Grade 12 Accountancy.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Unrecorded Assets and Liabilities
text:
Unrecorded Assets and Liabilities

Key terms: unrecorded assets, unrecorded liabilities, dissolution

Assets and liabilities that were not recorded in the books of accounts but are discovered and dealt with during the dissolution of a partnership firm.

metadata.subject: Accountancy
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Unrecorded Assets and Liabilities in Grade 12 Accountancy.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Firm's Debts vs Partner's Private Debts
text:
Firm's Debts vs Partner's Private Debts

Key terms: firm's debts, partner's private debts, dissolution

Firm's debts are liabilities incurred for the business, while partner's private debts are liabilities incurred by a partner for personal reasons. Both are treated differently during the dissolution of a partnership firm.

metadata.subject: Accountancy
metadata.topic: Firm's Debts vs Partner's Private Debts
metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to evaluate concepts related to Firm's Debts vs Partner's Private Debts in Grade 12 Accountancy.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Realisation Account vs Revaluation Account
text:
Realisation Account vs Revaluation Account

Key terms: realisation account, revaluation account, dissolution, valuation

Realisation account is used during the dissolution of a partnership firm to record the sale and realisation of assets and settlement of liabilities, while revaluation account is used to record changes in the value of assets and liabilities that are still in use.

metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to create concepts related to Realisation Account vs Revaluation Account in Grade 12 Accountancy.

Realisation Account

An account used to record the sale of assets and settlement of liabilities during the dissolution of a partnership.

Partner's Capital Account

An account that records each partner's initial investment, profits, losses, and final settlement during the dissolution of a partnership.

Bank Account

Profit Sharing Ratio

The ratio in which profits and losses are distributed among partners in a firm, determined by their initial investments or agreed terms.

metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Profit Sharing Ratio in Grade 12 Accountancy.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Realisation Loss/Gain
text:
Realisation Loss/Gain

The difference between the assets' realizable value and their book value, or the liabilities' settlement amount and their book value, during the dissolution of a partnership.

metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Realisation Loss/Gain in Grade 12 Accountancy.

Settlement of Liabilities

The process of paying off a firm's debts and other obligations during the dissolution of a partnership, often at a discount.

title: NCERT Grade 12 Accountancy | Commission on Realisation
text:
Commission on Realisation

A fee paid to a partner or an appointed person for managing the sale of assets and the settlement of liabilities during the dissolution of a partnership.

metadata.learning_objective: Students will be able to understand concepts related to Commission on Realisation in Grade 12 Accountancy.

Expenses of Realisation

The costs incurred during the sale of assets and the settlement of liabilities, such as legal fees, advertising, or other related expenses.
